usageNotes: Use this to modify the persistent configuration of an existing network interface on a node (IP, gateway, MTU, VLAN settings, bridge ports, bonding mode, etc.). Changes are written to `/etc/network/interfaces` but are NOT applied to the live network until you call the network reload endpoint (`put_nodes_node_network_reload`) or reboot the node — running traffic is uninterrupted until that apply step. Requires `Sys.Modify` on `/nodes/{node}`; the `type` parameter is mandatory even when you are only changing other fields.

examples.summary: Set a static IPv4 address and gateway on a Linux bridge, enable VLAN awareness, and ensure it autostart on boot

tips: Changes are staged only — always follow up with `put_nodes_node_network_reload` (applies via `ifreload -a`) or a node reboot to activate them.
Use the `delete` param (comma-separated config key names) to remove individual settings such as `gateway` or `bridge_vids` without recreating the interface from scratch.
Supplying `cidr` (e.g. '10.0.0.10/24') is equivalent to setting `address` + `netmask` separately; do not mix both forms for the same interface.
Bond mode `active-backup` requires `bond-primary` to be set to one of the slave interfaces for deterministic failover.

OVS parameters (`ovs_bridge`, `ovs_bonds`, `ovs_ports`, `ovs_tag`, `ovs_options`) are ignored unless the node has Open vSwitch installed and the interface `type` is one of OVSBridge/OVSBond/OVSPort/OVSIntPort.
